smells.finding: parse_episode() (scripts/apply_episode_delta.py:242-350) is ~110 lines including a nested parse_assertions() closure that itself has a flush()-based state machine; it handles header extraction, section-splitting, mechanical-field parsing, and nested-assertion parsing all in one function body. Not egregious, but past the point where extracting parse_assertions() (already a near-standalone closure) to a module-level function would sharpen it. Non-blocking refinement.

apply_delta() (line 693-708) and _dry_run_log() (line 819-833) both contain the identical 3-branch op-kind dispatch (if kind=='create': ... elif 'amend-assertion': ... elif 'retire': ...) verbatim. A shared _dispatch_ops(tx, ops) -> list[str] helper called by both would remove the duplication and the risk of the two dispatches drifting if a 4th op kind is ever added to only one of them.

override.repo_standard: docs/EPISODE_STORE.md section 4 (the frozen partition: 'the Mechanical bin ... Flat - key: value lines' naming the exact 9 mechanical fields as one bin)
override.reason: The 9 mechanical scalar fields (run/project/role/spine-step/context-manifest-ref/refusals/reopens/rework-count/failed-commands) always travel together because the frozen record grammar defines them as one bin with one allowlist (C2). Splitting them into a smaller value object would fight the contract this gate implements, not fix an accidental clump introduced by this code.

smells.finding: Every field is a plain str/int matching the flat '- key: value' Markdown grammar EPISODE_STORE.md section 3 specifies verbatim; using richer types would require serializing back to the same primitives at render time for no behavioral gain.

The one place shotgun surgery could bite -- binding the retirement layout at g4 -- is explicitly guarded against: all 5 layout-dependent seams (store_root is layout-invariant; iter_episode_ids, resolve_episode_path, apply_retirement/_retirement_destination, is_episode_in_ordinary_search, _new_episode_path) route through _LAYOUT_ADAPTER, verified by flipping the one constant in tests.

override.repo_standard: docs/EPISODE_STORE.md section 7 ('The full seam set' table and 'g2's writer ... must route every retire op through exactly one seam ... Both adapters share the identical content update')
override.reason: Both Option-A and Option-B adapters are implemented behind every layout seam even though only Option B is exercised in production today. This looks like unrequested flexibility, but the frozen upstream contract explicitly REQUIRES both adapters to exist now ('binding the layout at g4 means writing the four chosen adapters ... and wiring it in' implies both already exist pre-g4) so the layout decision can be held for human ratification without a later rewrite. The flexibility is mandated by the contract, not spec-crept by the implementer.

smells.finding: Comments consistently cite EPISODE_STORE.md section numbers to explain WHY, not to excuse unclear code; the code itself (dataclasses, small validate_* functions, the _Transaction class) reads clearly without the comments.
